description.narrative: The project “Women-led Green Livelihood Transformation in the Acidic Lowlands of the Mekong – Ninh Quoi, Ca Mau” empowers local women to develop sustainable and climate-resilient livelihoods. In this saline–acidic area, women are key to household economies but lack access to resources and decision-making. Implemented by the Mekong Institute – Can Tho University in partnership with the Center for Women’s Development, the 18-month project (11/2025–04/2027, budget EUR 59.872,12) aims to: (1) develop climate-adaptive green livelihoods; (2) strengthen women-led enterprises in production and finance; and (3) amplify women’s voices in policy dialogue. The initiative will directly benefit over 500 women and indirectly reach 3,000 people, promoting equitable, climate-resilient, and sustainable development in the Mekong’s acidic lowlands.

participating-org.narrative: The Mekong Institute was established upon the strong foundations of the former Mekong Delta Development Research Institute and the DRAGON-Mekong Institute. This consolidation represents a strategic milestone in advancing interdisciplinary research, capacity building, and regional collaboration for the sustainable development of the Mekong Delta and the broader Greater Mekong Subregion (GMS). As an interdisciplinary research and engagement hub, the Mekong Institute is dedicated to promoting sustainable development and climate resilience in deltaic and river basin systems. Guided by the LEAD vision: Learning to enhance knowledge, Engagement to foster inclusive collaboration, Advancement to apply science and technology for communities, and Development to support long-term, equitable growth, the Institute’s mission follows the RISE framework: conducting interdisciplinary Research, Integrating scientific and local knowledge, Supporting innovation in policy and technology, and Engaging diverse stakeholders in collaborative, multi-level action. With extensive experience, deep local insights, and an expanding network across sectors and borders, the Mekong Institute is well-positioned to contribute meaningfully through field-based research, science–policy engagement, and stakeholder-oriented training programs.
